newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate private eye firms agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate private eye firms agree to merge.

text.p: Decision Strategies International and Fairfax Group Ltd, two of the biggest U.S. firms in the field of private investigation, said Tuesday they will merge, continuing a trend to consolidation amid growing worldwide demand for business intelligence.
Terms of the transaction that will join the two closely-held firms were not disclosed.
The merger agreement followed by less than two weeks news that Kroll Associates, another leading investigative firm, would be acquired by O'Gara Co.
O'Gara is a maker of specialized security equipment. The Kroll firm is headed by veteran investigator Jules Kroll.

The combination of Decision Strategies and Fairfax will result in a firm of about 200 professionals operating from 20 offices in eight countries. The combined firm will be known as Decision Strategies/Fairfax International, LLC.

"Over the past year there has been an enormous demand for our investigative consulting services due to increased competition in the global marketplace, where the need to know who you are dealing with is paramount," Bart Schwartz, president and chief executive of New York-based Decision Strategies, said in a statement.

Schwartz will be president and chief executive of the new company. Michael Hershman, president of Fairfax, will be chairman of the merged firm. The merged firm will have its headquarters in New York and continue to have an office in Falls Church, Va., where Fairfax is located.

Investigative consulting firms help corporations carry out due diligence prior to merger agreements, check out potential hires for senior spots, conduct internal investigations, and advise on ways to prevent industrial espionage.

In a telephone interview, Schwartz, a former chief of the criminal division for the U.S. Attorney's office for the Southern District of New York, said he thought the timing of the Decision Strategies-Fairfax merger so soon after the Kroll deal was a coincidence.
"This is a merger whre we are not looking at reducing people, we are probalby in a hiring mode rather than anything else," he said referring to the Decision Strategies-Fairfax deal.

Hershman, who has had a variety of U.S. government investigative posts in Washington, said in the interview that the hottest areas at the moment are in due diligence for mergers, medical fraud, environmental cases and theft of trade secrets. He said a U.S. law enacted last year making it a crime to steal proprietary information prompted a significant rise in client inquiries.

Hershman and Schwartz declined to discuss financial terms of their merger or to estimate annual bilings of the combined firm. They said details of the merger will be completed by the end of September at the latest.
The merged firm is described by the participants as the largest independent investigative agency in the world.
